subject: English
central_question: How can a student choose and form the correct tense to show when an action happens and whether it is complete, continuing or repeated?
in_scope_units: Simple present: habitual actions, facts and general truths
Present continuous: actions happening now or temporary ongoing actions
Present perfect: completed actions at an unspecified past time or past actions continuing now
Present perfect continuous: actions continuing from the past into the present
Simple past: completed actions at a specific past time
Past continuous: actions in progress at a particular past time
Past perfect: actions completed before another past action
Past perfect continuous: actions continuing up to a past point
Simple future with will or shall
Future continuous for actions in progress at a future time
Future perfect for actions completed before a future point
Future perfect continuous for actions continuing up to a future point
Common errors involving specific past time, since/for and third-person singular agreement
banned_topics: Subject-verb concord beyond the third-person singular tense form

known_pitfalls.claim: Present perfect can be used with a finished past-time expression such as yesterday.
known_pitfalls.correction: A specific finished past time requires the simple past: 'I saw him yesterday,' not 'I have seen him yesterday.'

known_pitfalls.claim: Since and for can be used interchangeably.
known_pitfalls.correction: Use 'since' with a point in time and 'for' with a duration.

known_pitfalls.claim: The simple present uses the base verb for every subject.
known_pitfalls.correction: A third-person singular subject normally takes the verb ending -s or -es, as in 'She walks.'

recommended_example_progression: Fill in blanks using simple present and present continuous from time clues.
Correct present perfect and present perfect continuous sentences using has/have, since and for.
Choose among the four past tenses in a short sequence of events.
Complete future-time sentences using will, will be, will have and will have been.
Edit a mixed-tense passage containing typical CBSE errors.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: Typical CBSE practice includes fill-in-the-blanks, gap filling in passages, sentence completion, tense transformation and error correction.
